title: Students and teachers call for mobilisation and strikes over university funding
seoTitle: Paris student and teacher strike called

tea.why: Protesters say government responses to months of higher education protests are insufficient and cite a decade of austerity.
tea.want: They demand 150,000 university places, recruitment plans, increased funding, higher salaries, and the cancellation of Parcoursup.
tea.changed: Nov 23: An inter-union coalition of higher education staff and student organisations announced a nationwide strike and rallies for Nov 26.

summary: Following two months of protests, an inter-union coalition of higher education staff and student organisations has called for a nationwide day of strikes, rallies, and demonstrations. The coalition, including unions such as FSU, Unsa, CGT, SUD, FO, Unef, Union étudiante, FSE, Fage, and Solidaires étudiants, argues that government measures—including 20,000 newly announced university places—fall short of addressing years of funding shortages. Organisers demand the creation of 150,000 higher education places, a multi-year recruitment plan, increased budgets for universities and laboratories, higher student grants, staff salary increases, and the repeal of the Parcoursup and Mon Master systems. In response, the government previously announced 20,000 extra university places, plans to index student grants to inflation, and the eventual replacement of Parcoursup by 2028.
demands: Create 150,000 additional places in higher education
Implement a multi-year recruitment and tenure plan
Increase funding for universities and public laboratories
Revalue student grants and staff salaries
response: The government announced 20,000 additional higher education places, plans to evolve Parcoursup starting in 2027 before replacing it in 2028, and an indexation of student grants on inflation.

updates.text: An inter-union coalition of higher education staff and students called for a nationwide mobilisation and strikes on November 26.
